dataset_refs: round4 failed terminal cells: r4-03-baseline-8k, r4-06-baseline-8k, r4-08-index-8k
experiment_template.research_question: Does schema-bound no-effect terminal submission reduce invalid final outcomes while preserving evidence integrity and equal cumulative model-token caps?
stop_conditions: Any terminal submission performs a repository effect.
Any withheld or unknown source receives delivery credit.
Shared instrument or provider failure pauses unstarted cells.

success_criteria.treatment_valid_completions: at least 2 of 3 and at least one more than matched control

records.falsifier: Structured submission does not improve valid terminal outcomes on the frozen failure cohort, changes source credit, permits tool effects, exceeds equal model-token caps, or prevents actionable provenance diagnostics.
records.mechanism: During finalization expose one no-effect submit_context_selection action with closed summary and context_read_ids arguments; validate it with the same whole-envelope and source-provenance checks, and accept a valid call as the terminal candidate without requiring another model response.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash 8K exposed ContextBench development failures; terminal instrument only, before another evidence-index comparison.
records.statement: A schema-bound terminal submission action improves valid completion under small-window pressure.

experiment_template.research_question: Does a second bounded correction repair terminal failures within the same token cap?

records.falsifier: A second correction fails to improve completion, consumes the remaining budget before valid submission, or repeats the same invalid envelope.
records.mechanism: Keep free-form final JSON but reserve and permit a second validator-driven correction inside the same cumulative token cap.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash 8K exposed ContextBench development failures; terminal instrument only, before another evidence-index comparison.
records.statement: One additional diagnostic correction opportunity improves valid completion more than structured submission.

experiment_template.research_question: Are terminal failures unchanged when only submission shape changes?

records.falsifier: Structured terminal submission converts malformed or provenance-invalid controls into valid independently scored selections without new evidence delivery.
records.mechanism: The model lacks or misidentifies relevant pinned-base evidence; changing the terminal wire shape only moves the same invalid IDs into tool arguments.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash 8K exposed ContextBench development failures; terminal instrument only, before another evidence-index comparison.
records.statement: The remaining failures are semantic source-selection failures that structured serialization cannot repair.

selection.reason: Two of three observed failures are invalid JSON, making schema-bound submission the most direct discriminating mechanism. It also preserves the whole-envelope validator for the provenance failure. A second correction changes both budget and retry count, so it remains an alternative.
